meta.instrument: script/m14/incoming-gate.ts (single whole-population measurement; this declaration is DERIVED from its own TABLE 1 by script/m14/css-declaration.ts, which refuses on any non-closure)

populationRule.rule: the admitted set is the GIT-TRACKED set: per-checkout `git ls-files` over $PWD/.corpus, extensions css,less,sass from the router's one table, files present on disk and at most 1 MiB

meta.resolvedScope: the file's OWN PROJECT (production's scope; index=no — the analyzer sees one file at a time, and the arbiter holds the project)

imports_targets_outside_the_admitted_set.what: the `imports` row's unresolved targets are stylesheet specifiers whose files are NOT in the admitted set (a relative path out of the repository, or a bare package name). An `@import` names a stylesheet the run cannot open, so no declaration in this population can answer it — the count is the arm's own unresolved column for the type.

falsifier.run: npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts css 0 (the whole-population arm; TABLE 1's imports unresolved column is the count)
falsifier.wouldFail: a run in which one of those specifiers resolves — that would mean the target IS in the admitted set and the row belongs in resolved.

references_custom_property_declared_else.what: the `references` row's ambiguous tail is CUSTOM PROPERTIES declared more than once across the project (`--color-cd-punctuation`, `--color-cd-builtin`, …): a `var(--x)` read names a property whose declaration site cannot be chosen from the name alone, which is the tie-break the arbiter applies, not a defect in this lane.

falsifier.run: npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts css 0 (TABLE 1's references ambiguous column is the count; the worklist prints the names)
falsifier.wouldFail: a run in which those names resolve to ONE declaration — that would mean the ambiguity was the run's resolution mode, not the corpus's name collisions.

part_of_targets_naming_no_carried_file.what: the `part_of` row's non-resolved tail is plain-file-form `@import` specifiers that name a file the admitted set does not carry (`minireset`, `generic`, `animations`, `breadcrumb`) plus ONE ambiguous name (`table`, six declarations of the type). The census measured the same split from the other side: of 126 plain-file-form sites, 114 name a carried file and 12 name nothing admitted.

falsifier.run: npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts css 0 (TABLE 1's part_of columns; the worklist prints the names)
falsifier.wouldFail: a run in which one of those specifiers resolves — that would move it into resolved and shrink this count.

resolution_caveats: A CAUSE IS STATED, NOT RESOLVED: unresolved rows live in otherUnresolved (which also holds the binding-spelled and declared-cause rows), never in resolved, and the analyzer's scope is PER FILE with index=no — a target declared in another file of the project is genuinely out of its reach and the arbiter (which holds the project) is what answers it.
`contains` and `uses` resolve to nodes of the SAME file, so their resolved buckets mean what the bucket means everywhere: this file declares the name.

`references` carries the custom-property reads (161,768 of them) whose target is a custom property NAME: a resolved reference says a declaration of that name exists in this file, not that it is the read's only source.

`part_of` rows are the plain-file-form `@import` inclusions; their target is the included stylesheet's project-relative name, and 383-class resolution behaviour is CSS-family: a header need not declare a symbol named after itself, which is why 12 of the 126 plain-file sites name nothing admitted.

`calls` and `exports` are IMPLEMENTED AND CORPUS-UNEXERCISED: the analyzer emits them from the grammar's own shapes (`@function --name` declarations and the CSS Modules `:export` block) and this population exercises neither, so both publish measured zero rows with fixture css/calls-and-exports as the live positive control.
